newsitem.title: GERMANY: German CDU mulling ways to bind Italy into EMU.
newsitem.headline: German CDU mulling ways to bind Italy into EMU.

text.p: Foreign policy experts from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) are looking at ways of binding Italy into European monetary union (EMU) while delaying Rome's entry, party sources said on Tuesday.

But the sources played down a news agency report that ideas to make Italy a founder state while delaying full Italian membership of EMU to 2002 -- when the euro will be issued as a cash currency -- had the status of a German government plan.
"This should not be treated as a government position," one source told Reuters on condition of anonymity.

Germany wants EMU to go ahead on time in 1999 with a first wave of hard currency states, and both political leaders and Bundesbank officials have called for a strict interpretation of Maastricht treaty criteria for entry.
